name: Ranger Freerunner
body:
Experiencing the exhilaration of unfettered running is a freerunner’s greatest pleasure. Freerunners excel at moving rapidly through their environment, negotiating obstacles (living and inanimate) by employing a variety of acrobatic maneuvers including jumping, climbing, and somersaulting.

A freerunner has the following class features.

Class Skills

A freerunner gains Acrobatics and Perform (tumble).

This alters class skills.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

A freerunner is proficient with all simple and martial weapons, and with one light or one handed exotic weapon of his choice. He is not proficient with any armor or shields.

This alters weapon and armor proficiency.

Astute Maneuverability (Ex)

When unarmored and unencumbered, a freerunner adds his Wisdom bonus (if any) to his AC and CMD. In addition, a freerunner gains a +1 bonus to AC and CMD at 4th level.

This bonus increases by 1 for every four freerunner levels thereafter, up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. These bonuses to AC apply even against touch attacks or when the freerunner is flat-footed. He loses these bonuses when he is immobilized or helpless, when he wears any armor, when he carries a shield, or when he carries a medium or heavy load. (A multiclass freerunner with levels in monk treats his monk levels as freerunner levels for the purpose of determining when the +1 bonuses to AC/CMD are gained.) A freerunner that takes levels in another class that adds the character’s Intelligence (or Charisma) modifier to its AC while unarmored and unencumbered treats that class ability and astute maneuverability as one and the same for stacking purposes, and therefore must choose one or the other to add, but cannot add both.

Furthermore, a freerunner can use his Wisdom modifier rather than his Dexterity modifier on his Acrobatics and Perform (tumble) skill check rolls. Once this choice is made, it is permanent and cannot be changed.

Fueled by Adrenaline (Ex)

At 1st level, a freerunner gains a pool of adrenaline points, which provide him with short bursts of energy, allowing him to accomplish amazing feats. The number of points in a freerunner’s adrenaline pool is equal to 1/2 his freerunner level (minimum 1) + his Wisdom modifier. As long as a freerunner has at least 1 point in his adrenaline pool, he reduces the DC for any Acrobatics skill checks by 2 points, does not suffer any penalty to Acrobatics checks for obstructed or sloped conditions, and is always treated as having a running start when attempting an Acrobatics check to jump.

By spending 1 point from his adrenaline pool as an immediate action when required to make a Reflex saving throw roll, a freerunner gains a +1 competence bonus to that roll. This bonus increases by +1 for every five freerunner levels, to a maximum of +5 at 20th level.

This, in conjunction with adrenaline powers, replaces favored enemy, quarry, and improved quarry.

Adrenaline Powers (Ex)

Some adrenaline powers are constantly in effect, requiring no expenditure of points from the freerunner’s adrenaline pool, while others require the freerunner to expend 1 or more points to activate. Once an adrenaline power is selected, it cannot be changed. Some adrenaline powers require the freerunner to be of a specific level or higher before they can be chosen. A freerunner cannot select an adrenaline power more than once. A freerunner loses the use of his adrenaline powers if he wears any armor or carries a medium or heavy load.

At 1st level, a freerunner can select 1 adrenaline power.

At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, the freerunner can select 1 additional adrenaline power. At 11th level, and again at 19th level, a freerunner can choose to either add +2 points to his adrenaline pool or select 1 additional adrenaline power.

This, in conjunction with fueled by adrenaline, replaces favored enemy, quarry, and improved quarry.

Adrenaline Surge (Ex)

A freerunner with this power can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a swift action to grant himself a sudden burst of speed. This increases the freerunner’s base land speed by 30 feet for 1 minute.

Constant Motion (Ex)

When a freerunner with this power would normally be hit with a melee attack, he can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as an immediate action to gain a free Acrobatics check (DC = the attack roll that hit the freerunner) to deflect some or all of the blow. A freerunner suffers 1/2 damage (round down) on a successful Acrobatics check, and no damage if the Acrobatics check exceeds the DC by 5 or more. A freerunner must be at least 10th level before selecting this adrenaline power.

Effortless Descent (Ex)

A freerunner with this power does not need to expend adrenaline points from his adrenaline pool to activate it; its effects are constantly active. Whenever the freerunner falls (intentionally or not), a successful DC 15 Acrobatics check allows him to ignore the first 30 feet fallen. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, this distance increases by an additional 20 feet.

Expedited Assault (Ex)

A freerunner with this power can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a swift action to increase his offensive capabilities; when taking the fullattack action, he gains 1 extra attack at his highest base attack bonus for 1 round. This extra attack stacks with the extra attack gained from the spell haste, but does not stack with extra attacks granted by the class ability flurry of blows.

A freerunner must be at least 5th level before selecting this adrenaline power.

Perfect Agility (Ex)

A freerunner with this power can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a swift action to gain a +5 competence bonus to all Acrobatics checks. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +5, to a maximum of +25 at 20th level. If a freerunner spends 2 points rather than 1 when activating this power, he gains additional benefits; he can move at full speed while making an Acrobatics check to move across a narrow surface without adding +5 to the DC of the check, and he can move through a threatened square to avoid provoking an attack of opportunity from an enemy without adding +10 to the DC. This effect lasts for 1 minute.

Quick-Up (Ex)

A freerunner with this power does not need to expend adrenaline points from his adrenaline pool to activate it; its effects are constantly active, allowing a freerunner to use a swift action to stand from a prone position without provoking an attack of opportunity for standing while threatened by an enemy.

Ricocheting Ascent (Ex)

A freerunner with this power does not need to expend adrenaline points from his adrenaline pool to activate it; its effects are constantly active, allowing a freerunner to walk on walls for brief distances. A freerunner can use a single move action to traverse a wall or other vertical surface if he begins and ends his movement on a horizontal surface. The height achieved on the wall is limited only by this movement restriction. If a freerunner does not end his move on a horizontal surface capable of supporting his weight, he falls. The wall is treated as a normal floor for the purposes of measuring movement. Passing from floor to wall costs no movement; a freerunner can change services freely. A freerunner can expend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a free action to gain the benefits of this power until the end of his current turn.

Unrestricted (Ex)

A freerunner with this power can spend 1 point from his adrenaline pool as a free action to gain unrestricted movement; he is treated as though under the effects of freedom of movement for 10 minutes. A freerunner must be at least 10th level before selecting this adrenaline power.

Whirlwind Assault (Ex)

A freerunner with this power can spend 2 points from his adrenaline pool as a swift action to gain the benefits of the feat Whirlwind Attack for 1 round. A freerunner must be at least 10th level before selecting this adrenaline power.

Motivation (Ex)

At 1st level, a freerunner selects 1 motivating force behind his love for running freely across a multitude of terrains.

Each motivation comes with its own unique benefit. Once made, this selection is permanent, and cannot be changed.

Ducking the Law (Ex)

You have either personally experienced time behind bars, or you have acted as a vigilante, taking the law into your own hands to free individuals you believed were wrongly incarcerated. You gain Disable Device as a class skill and can add 1/2 your freerunner level to Disable Device skill checks made to open locks.

Free-spirited (Ex)

You were born with an exuberance for fast-paced movement. You gain fast movement as the barbarian ability of the same name. At 8th level, your speed is increased by +20 feet instead of +10 feet.

Tricks of the Trade (Ex)

You were either a street performer, a high-wire or trapeze artist with a traveling circus, or a professional athlete competing in local seasonal games. You can use Perform (tumble) checks in place of Acrobatics and Climb skill checks, and you gain a +2 competence bonus on Perform (tumble) skill checks.

This replaces track and swift tracker.

Wilderness Magic (Sp)

At 1st level, a freerunner selects 3 0-level spells (orisons) from the druid spell list. Once made, this selection is permanent, and cannot be changed. The freerunner can cast these spells as a spell-like ability, in any combination, a number of times per day equal to his Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). At 4th level, a freerunner can use his wilderness magic spell-like ability an unlimited number of times per day.

This replaces wild empathy.

Combat Style Feat (Ex)

A freerunner adds a new category of combat styles to the options he can select from called skirmisher. If a freerunner selects skirmisher as his combat style, he can choose from the following list whenever he gains a combat style feat: Acrobatic Steps, Dodge, Fleet, and Nimble Moves. At 6th level, he adds Landing Roll, Mobility, and Spring Attack to the list. At 10th level, he adds Acrobatic SpellcasterUI and Disorienting Maneuver to the list. This ability functions as combat style feat in all other ways.

This alters combat style feat.

Run

At 3rd level, a freerunner gains the bonus feat Run.

This replaces endurance.

Topographical Bond (Ex)

At 4th level, a freerunner can select an animal companion following the standard rules for a ranger’s hunter’s bond, or he can elect to bond with his favored terrains. If he selects the latter, a freerunner gains a +2 insight bonus to his AC in all of his favored terrains. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +1.

This alters hunter’s bond.

Perpetual Motion (Ex)

At 20th level, a freerunner can select 1 of his adrenaline powers that requires the expenditure of adrenaline points to activate. The freerunner can activate this power without expending adrenaline points a number of times per day equal to 3 + the freerunner’s Wisdom modifier. Additionally, a freerunner can take an additional move action in the current round a number of times per day equal to his Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

This replaces master hunter.
